# Scribl Shape Review -- Retro (2026-09-04)

Durable retro of the 2026-09-04 Shape Review. Same exception as the
2026-07-14 and 2026-08-25 workshop retros: a client review is durable
knowledge, not an operational record. The operational digest and
action-item seam live at
[`knowledge/meetings/2026-09-04-shape-review.md`](../../meetings/2026-09-04-shape-review.md);
the raw transcript is preserved internally at
`knowledge/meetings/raw/2026-09-04-shape-review.vtt` (not in the rendered
site).

**Format:** Teams call, about 45 minutes (first cue 00:00:17, last cue ends
00:44:47) against a scheduled 60-minute slot. Facilitator: Rob Forshier II,
running a prepared talk track
(`artifacts/shape-review-2026-09-04.html`) rather than a formal deck.

| Side | People |
| --- | --- |
| Scribl | Eric Rice, Matthew Kaplan |
| Bounteous | Rob Forshier II (facilitation, demo), Pankaj Aggarwal (engineering lead) |

Only these four speak in the transcript. The invite also included Pramod
Kumar, David Lawton, Martin Young, John Kilgore and Angie Yap; none of them
appear with a speaker turn. Treat that as unconfirmed attendance, not
absence -- Rob told Pankaj at the open that most of the India-side invite
list was optional ("I honestly didn't think you were going to be here...
You didn't actually have to show up," 00:00:19).

This is the page Rob asked for by name: lead with the questions and the
follow-ups, because that is what the review actually produced.

## Questions raised, and their follow-ups

- **Where in the wiki can Eric point Scribl's patent/IP lawyers for a
  snapshot of the architecture and framework?** Raised by Eric Rice
  (00:23:54): the patent process is underway and lawyers will ask "where is
  this, how is this built, what's the framework." No such page exists yet.
  **Follow-up, owner Eric Rice:** send Rob the full outline of what the
  lawyers need; Rob will build a dedicated page from it (00:24:44 to
  00:25:10). No date committed.
- **How should the IP boundary between Bounteous's internal Arc platform,
  Anthropic, and the custom-built harness be explained to counsel?** Raised
  by Matthew Kaplan (00:25:14) immediately after Eric's question, tied to
  the SOW/MSA IP terms he and Scribl's attorney "Marty" had already worked
  through. Rob answered live and precisely: nothing shipped on this project
  came from Bounteous's Arc IP; everything is custom Claude harnesses Rob
  built personally, following Bounteous's internal conventions (00:26:03 to
  00:26:45). **Follow-up, owner Matthew Kaplan:** loop in Marty, and
  possibly set up a direct call between Rob and two names heard as "Ed" and
  "Nidhi" (spelling unconfirmed in the transcript) so Rob can speak to
  counsel directly rather than through relayed messages (00:27:09 to
  00:27:19). Rob agreed and asked for an advance question list so he can
  prepare (00:27:19 to 00:27:30). No date committed.
- **What capability snapshot does the eventual internal dev hire need to
  onboard quickly?** Raised by Eric Rice (00:27:43), on behalf of Scribl
  contacts "Marty, Sanju and some friends over at AWS" who are helping
  identify that hire. **Follow-up, owner Rob Forshier II:** offered to
  generate a written capability/tech-stack summary, and even a job
  description, directly from the meta-repo's query tooling once asked
  (00:28:15 to 00:28:58). Unassigned as to when -- Rob's offer is
  on-request, not scheduled.
- **Where does delivery stand against the original timeline?** Raised by
  Matthew Kaplan (00:36:58), framed explicitly as curiosity rather than a
  commitment ask. Rob does not have a precise answer yet -- the backlog was
  only produced the day or two prior and is still being reconciled against
  actual progress. **Follow-up, owner Rob Forshier II:** a firmer read by
  end of next week, 2026-09-11 (00:37:19 to 00:37:39). Rob's directional
  read in the meantime: the team is well ahead on the front end, with less
  certainty once the rest of the team's velocity is established
  (00:37:47 to 00:38:00).
- **At what point should Scribl bring on a fractional product owner (a
  candidate the team calls "Allison")?** Raised by Matthew Kaplan
  (00:38:14 to 00:39:03). Rob's answer: probably not until the later
  sprints of the beta, and even then it might be early, since there isn't
  enough for a PO to do yet and onboarding overhead needs weighing against
  timing (00:39:09 to 00:39:39). Matthew: "that's helpful, makes sense"
  (00:39:40). No decision, no date -- an estimate, held open until Scribl
  has the candidate available.

## Decisions made -- design (Christina's mockups)

Eric walked five mockup screens Christina produced (main/home, login,
canvas, share, and home-screen variants), framed as final except for a few
named rollbacks and open items. Owner for every row below is Eric Rice
unless noted; these are calls made live in the room, not a formal client
sign-off document.

| # | Screen | Decision | Cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Main/home | Go with the second mockup option; tone pitched as a "Goldilocks" between the existing prototype and the B2B game -- less intense than B2B, more flair than the prototype; fonts, sizing, hierarchy, logos match the brand book | 00:20:20 to 00:20:45 |
| 2 | Login | Go with the middle option; wants the gradient background if technically possible | 00:30:47 to 00:31:04 |
| 3 | Home layout | Roll back Christina's two-page swipe (stats and walls on separate pages) to the current single-page layout, walls stacked under stats -- simpler for MVP | 00:31:12 to 00:31:35 |
| 4 | Home: wall icon canvas | Keep the wall-icon dimensions matching the drawing canvas as a **future** option (draw a custom mascot/logo per wall, like avatars); explicitly not MVP | 00:31:37 to 00:31:57 |
| 5 | Home: activity indicators | "Seven new drawings" style badges are present in the mockup; Eric can have them removed if Bounteous does not want them -- not firmly decided either way | 00:31:59 to 00:32:12 |
| 6 | Home: "see more" stats deep-dive | Cut from MVP; kept as a future idea (Spotify Wrapped-style stats sharing) | 00:34:13 to 00:34:35 |
| 7 | Home: "trending" affirmations | Cut from MVP; kept as a future idea pending a data point to compute it from | 00:34:35 to 00:34:59 |
| 8 | Home: draw button size | Shrink the oversized draw button to match the other two nav buttons | 00:35:00 to 00:35:17 |
| 9 | Share screen | Go with blue; logo larger, lower right, matching the current share treatment | 00:35:18 to 00:35:37 |
| 10 | Share screen: date | Remove the date/prompt-day stamp -- unneeded since a share can happen at any time | 00:35:38 to 00:35:47 |
| 11 | Canvas controls | Go with the two-line control layout: undo and trash stretched across one line, a single "I'm done" action on the line below -- chosen over one line to avoid mis-taps on small color swatches (a recurring B2B complaint); willing to revert to one line if the two-line layout is spatially a problem | 00:35:50 to 00:36:33 |

Not fully decided, held open:

- **Activity-indicator badges** ("new drawings" counts) -- present in the
  mockup, removable on request, no firm call either way (00:31:59).
- **Canvas control layout space** -- two lines is the stated preference,
  but Eric flagged willingness to fall back to one line if space does not
  work in practice (00:36:33).

No design-decision item in this session was checked against the ratified
decision register (`product/inputs/reference/decisions/`) during the call
itself -- the talk track's block 2 was built for that purpose, but the
conversation stayed at the screen-and-layout level and did not reference
specific ADRs by number. None of the decisions above appear to contradict
the register on their face (canvas remains Skia-based per ADR 0006; nothing
here touches backend, data-layer, or moderation ADRs), but that comparison
was not made explicit in the transcript, so it is not asserted here as
checked.

## Sprint accomplishments credited

Rob's walkthrough, in the order given, with the person he credited:

- **Pramod Kumar** -- delivery management: staffing an iOS engineer swap
  for a family emergency, coordinating with Pankaj, and driving the
  GitHub/AWS/Apple access emails with Eric (00:03:48 to 00:04:27).
- **Pankaj Aggarwal** -- engineering practice: architecture layers,
  dependency rules, CI/CD and GitHub Actions, the ratified wiki inside the
  Scribl app repo, a `pnpm bootstrap` script that installs all dependencies
  in one command, a developer-setup/local-setup wiki page, and onboarding
  pages for a future hire. Backend is close, blocked only on AWS wiring
  (00:04:44 to 00:08:33, 00:47:47 to 00:50:44).
- **Nitish Goyal** (named, not present) -- reworked the prototype's API
  contracts into production endpoints, PR merged (00:08:43 to 00:09:15).
- **Karuna** (named, not present) -- defining QA test patterns, to
  eventually be baked into the team's Claude skills so tests get written
  consistently as part of the SLT process (00:09:18 to 00:10:23).
- **Shubh(ankar)** (named, not present) -- iOS platform work alongside
  Pankaj (00:10:29 to 00:10:51).
- **Rob Forshier II** -- rejiggered the prototype to match the redesigned
  invite/onboarding flow (about 3 days of the sprint), built the new
  compose (image-composite) screen from scratch off Eric's live demo, kept
  the backlog and wiki current, and built out the meta-repo's meeting-ingest
  automation this session is itself an example of (00:12:39 to 00:22:36).
- Rob also live-demoed the Scribl app running locally (web build, iOS build
  blocked on his own missing Apple account setup), confirming it is already
  front-end production-ready against a mock backend (00:18:37 to 00:22:30).
  Pankaj confirmed: "it is production ready... in terms of security, code
  quality, everything, it's top notch" for the front end; backend is close,
  pending AWS (00:01:15 to 00:01:50).

## Process retro

Both client attendees gave positive process feedback with one specific
critique:

- **Eric Rice:** the process feels different from prior builds -- "learning
  a lot more and feel more involved," rather than passively directing a dev
  team (00:40:35 to 00:40:54). Later: this build feels like a strong
  foundation for growth rather than a rush to MVP, which matters because
  Scribl wants to build this much bigger (00:41:31 to 00:43:59).
- **Matthew Kaplan:** excited, feels fast-moving, but flagged that early
  live workshop sessions (sticky-note, drag-and-drop) put the Scribl team
  on the spot without advance notice of the topics, producing groupthink
  rather than considered input (00:41:06 to 00:41:47). **Decision, owner
  Rob Forshier II:** send session/board links earlier ahead of future
  live sessions so the team has time to prepare (00:42:04 to 00:42:11).
- **Pankaj Aggarwal:** the same structured, automated approach used for the
  meta-repo and wiki is being mirrored on the coding side -- harness prompts
  for consistent Claude-generated code, automated guardrails
  (00:42:18 to 00:43:01).
